R.DraR1 is a well-studied endonuclease from the radiation-resistant bacterium *D. radiodurans*. In characterization studies of this enzyme, various divalent cations were tested for their effects on cleavage activity. While Mg2+ serves as the standard cofactor for many nucleases, studies on R.DraR1 specifically demonstrated that **Mn2+** had the strongest enhancing effect on its cleavage activity, surpassing the effect of Mg2+ and other tested divalent ions.
